newsitem.title: USA: US debt futures end higher, Eurodollars lead gains.
newsitem.headline: US debt futures end higher, Eurodollars lead gains.

text.p: U.S. debt futures closed higher, with Eurodollars leading gains on flight-to-quality buying after Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's comments eased market concerns about higher U.S. rates, traders said.
"Greenspan didn't say anything new, but it was interesting what he didn't say," one debt futures market analyst said. "He didn't say inflation pressures were imminent."

The market focused on Greenspan's comment that he saw scant signs now of an imminent resurgence of inflation, rather than his statement that the U.S. central bank would need to act if growth fails to slow as expected.
Most Eurodollar contracts held gains even during the dollar rout, which pressured June T-bonds to 109-19/32.

Bond futures traders said the dollar's decline to 119.00 spot against the yen, coupled with the technical failure of June bonds to rally above the two-month high of 110-14/32, pushed the contract to session lows.

They said dollar/yen selling, as well as fears the dollar was topping out against other currencies, led to long liquidation. Talk circulated that some foreign investors were selling dollar-denominated assets.
Technically, floor traders said June bonds had to fill a chart gap left-over from overnight trade.
Some funds, which had loaded up on long positions on Thursday and early Friday, decided to take profits as well.
Thin volume exacerbated the June bond's slide to 109-19/32 from the two-month highs, they said.
However, June gravitated above the 200-day moving average of 110-02/32 before the close, which improved the near-term technical outlook.

At the end of pit trade, June T-bonds were up 13/32 at 110-07/32, 10-year notes were up 11/32 at 107-13/32, munibonds were 16/32 higher at 115-25/32, September T-bills were up 0.085 at 94.52, September Eurodollars were up 0.085 at 93.93 and December Eurodollars were up 0.095 at 93.72. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
